messages.subject: Re: ping 3
messages.body_plain:
Hi Claudia,

This is the reply from Lei Jiang, whose project is R-OpenMP. Now the first-stage work is done to add pragma-style comments to any serial code and my parser can convert it to a parallel version. By next week, I will finish this part by implementing more such pragma to improve the compatibility and functionality on parallel computing.

We plan to switch to more backend-oriented development in the second half of GSoC'2011, which will require more C/C++/Fortran programming and pay more attention in performance/benchmarking.

Regards,
Lei

messages.subject: midterm evaluations
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

please fill in the midterm evaluations - deadline is Friday and missing
evaluations are counted as fail by Google. This applies to students as
well as to mentors.

Each project needs to have one student and at least one mentor
evaluation. Google now allows for more than one official mentor per
student, so I entered the co-mentors: Co-mentors should be able to do
the evaluation as well.

If you cannot access the evaluation form (table evaluations on the
dashboard) please let us admins know.
So far, we can see that about half of the projects have the mentor
evaluations submitted already - thank you!
We cannot see whether the students submitted their evaluations.

Best,

Claudia

--

messages.subject: Re: UseR! call for late posters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Claudia,

I'm attaching the abstract for the poster that we'll present at UseR2011 on the Manipulate GSoC project.    Randall Pruim, a collaborator on the MOSAIC project, will be making the presentation.   JJ Allaire, co-mentor for the GSoC project, will also be there.

We're also preparing a presentation for the Joint Math Meetings in January 2012 in Boston.  Our plan is to have Andrew Rich, the GSoC student, make the presentation there.  It was infeasible to send him to UseR2011.

Regards,
Danny

messages.subject: Mentor summit in October
messages.body_plain:
Mentors should have received a msg from Carol Smith at Google about the Mentor Summit in
October. Each Org gets to send 2 people.

Google pays us $2000 for travel to the event, and they supply hotel (individual rooms) and
food for the Fri night - Sunday afternoon event. We already have one request from European
location, so someone a bit closer who wants to go should let Claudia and I know ASAP.
We're in process of registering for the P.O. with Google so R can get paid. FYI,
reimbursement is pretty slow -- in my case last year about 3 months, but I did get paid
eventually. (However, in meantime the C$ had risen, but that's another story.)

I can attest that the event is interesting, though R tends to be an outlier compared to
other FLOSS organizations.

Best, JN
